newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU farm reform to focus on spending.
newsitem.headline: EU farm reform to focus on spending.

text.p: The focus of a policy paper being prepared by European Union farm Commissoner Franz Fischler on the future of the Common Agriculture Policy (CAP) will focus on defending existing budget levels, Commission sources said.
"The Commissioner's most important target is to maintain the agricultural guideline at least at its existing level beyond the end of the century," a source said.
There is no guarantee that the guideline will be topped up, as it was after the previous enlargement of the EU, when the first of the central European applicant countries join.
Currently the agricultural guideline is 40 billion ecus a year which will rise to 46 billion under present arrangements by the end of the decade.
Fischler will be battling finance ministers to keep the status quo of funding which limits the annual budget increase to 74 per cent of any increase in EU gross domestic product.
Driving change to the way agricultural spending is applied is the forthcoming round of World Trade Organisation (WTO) talks due to start in 1999.
Fischler is known to be angry that both France and Germany opposed including the Cork declaration on regional rural development in the December Dublin summit conclusions.
Both countries fear that a move towards regional support could lead to cuts in agricultural funding for farmers and a running down of the CAP.

"Those who oppose a regional policy, designed to give more general support, risk seeing agricultural spending run down as a result of American pressure in the WTO without any guarantee for the alternative regional option," a source explained.
